A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Ctrl-U. Their complete main text, equations, tables, figures and supplementary material are readable and can be matched despite appendix renumbering and an added figure.

before.justification: v1 reports original conditional-generation benchmarks, hyperparameter ablations, a 20-participant human evaluation and supplementary generated-image examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds qualitative examples comparing estimated uncertainty with reward-model errors in Figure 6.

M1.justification: The two-forward estimator, KL/L1 uncertainty measures and loss equations remain unchanged. However, Figure 2 replaces the fire-marked Diffusion block with a snowflake-marked UNet. The unchanged training descriptions do not resolve whether this corrects the schematic or changes which weights are optimized.

E1.justification: Both evaluate ADE20K and COCO-Stuff segmentation controls and MultiGen-20M HED, LineArt and depth controls. The added uncertainty visualization examines existing segmentation coverage rather than introducing a dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: Tables 1–4 and Figure 3 retain the same comparison methods, including the SDXL entries in Table 1 and reimplemented ControlNet++ CLIP-score row in Table 3. Additional citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 and Table 5's caption change the recommended timestep threshold from 1 to 400, agreeing with the existing Table 5b results. The tested threshold grid, dataset splits, metrics, sampling settings and training budgets remain unchanged; this correction does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Section 5.2 and Figure 6 provide three qualitative diagnostics comparing generated images, true conditions, reward predictions and uncertainty maps. They examine whether high uncertainty identifies incorrect rewards. The original hyperparameter ablations and uncertainty-training comparison remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over four generated-image groups in Tables 1–3. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests. Its new uncertainty maps depict method outputs rather than statistical uncertainty in experimental results.

E6.justification: Table 5 changes the selected configuration's CLIP-score from 30.89 to 31.26 in all four subtables, now matching Table 3 and changing some within-ablation rankings. Figure 6 adds qualitative uncertainty/error findings. The numerical results in Tables 1–4 and 6 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7, including the uncertainty definitions and regularized objective, are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added; the new material is explanatory and qualitative.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims: uncertainty-aware reward modeling mitigates inaccurate feedback and improves controllability and image quality across segmentation, edge and depth controls.

C2.justification: The introduction more specifically attributes reward errors to noise-induced distribution discrepancy and diffusion compression. Section 5.2 adds an interpretation connecting spatial uncertainty with unreliable reward feedback. Existing applicability boundaries and proposed future extensions to pose and scribbles remain.

D1.justification: The abstract changes a promised code/models/demo release into a statement that code is publicly available, with an explicit project address. Conversely, Section 4.1 removes the disclosure of eight A100 80GB GPUs. Dataset construction and reward/evaluation-model details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to FairDiff, Multi-reward as Condition, Diffusion-based Visual Anagram and VL-Uncertainty, while removing BLIP-Diffusion and TextDiffuser. Related-work explanations receive limited updates without substantially redefining Ctrl-U's positioning.

P1.justification: There are localized introduction and related-work rewrites, expanded explanations, authorship-note updates and a new acknowledgement. Supplementary sections A.1 and A.2 become 5.1 and 5.3 around the added Section 5.2; the main narrative structure remains.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with revised module and trainability annotations, Figures 2–4 receive expanded captions, and uncertainty Figure 6 is added. Figure 5 and Table 6 are repositioned; the original supplementary image grids remain as Figures 7–10. Table rules and spacing also receive limited adjustments.

improvement.justification: The added uncertainty/error visualization provides modest support for the central mechanism, while the corrected threshold description and consistent selected-setting CLIP scores improve clarity. The primary benchmark evidence remains unchanged. These gains outweigh limited documentation drawbacks: the removed GPU specification and the unexplained change in Figure 2's trainability symbols.
